newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Antwerp-based VLM buys three Fokker 50 aircraft.
newsitem.headline: Antwerp-based VLM buys three Fokker 50 aircraft.

text.p: VLM (Vlaamse Luchttransportmaatschappij), an Antwerp-based airline, has acquired three Fokker 50 aircraft, said the company's sales and marketing manager, Herman Vermeiren.
This brings the airline's total fleet to seven aircraft. VLM operates scheduled services from Antwerp, Rotterdam and Munchengladbach Airport to London City.
The three-year-old airline is privately owned by Jaap Rosen Jacobsen, a Dutch entrepreneur.

Initially the three new planes will not be joining the VLM fleet but Vermeiren declined to reveal where they will be deployed. However, they will eventually join VLM and will be used to start new routes, he said. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
